decision: Include, with an extended subgroup label
rationale: Stable categories, scope descriptions and grouping structures meet a broad definition of knowledge organization. Their objects are economic, medical or occupational statistical units rather than general library subjects; comparisons with general-purpose KOS must preserve that distinction.
related_resources: ISIC; NACE; NAICS; ICD; COICOP; COFOG; SITC; HS; ISCO

lead: National editions, language editions and revisions
decision: Merge within the same system
rationale: Translations, national extensions, years and file formats do not increase the candidate count. Independently developed systems such as NDC, CLC and RVK are not treated as language mirrors of DDC.
related_resources: DDC; NDC; CLC; ICD; ISCO; HS

decision: Access channels, not additional KOS
rationale: Software services that access or manage the same knowledge organization resource do not become distinct systems because their interfaces differ.

decision: Record distinct layers within one system
rationale: The Foundation is the underlying semantic structure; MMS is its principal statistical linearization. Splitting views does not increase the system count this round.

decision: Merge into ICF
rationale: WHO states that ICF-CY has been merged back into ICF and is no longer supported separately.

decision: Include as a historical candidate and mark discontinued maintenance
rationale: A distinct classification identity and hierarchical structure are verifiable. Discontinued maintenance affects later selection but does not erase the system's identity.

decision: Separate CPC-Patent and CPC-Product
rationale: The former is the EPO/USPTO patent technology classification; the latter is the UN product statistical classification. They are not versions of one system.

decision: Merge by framework this round
rationale: Internal components of a framework are described without inflating system counts. Later research may separate them by analytical unit.

decision: Record only as a related tool; no separate count this round
rationale: WIPO states that although EPIC is based on Locarno, it is not the official classification text. It is noted as a browsing aid to avoid counting an auxiliary extension and its main classification twice.

decision: Not distinct KOS in this group
rationale: GTIN identifies trade items, while DDD is a dose-statistics unit. Neither constitutes a separate subject-category system for this round. The classification resources are GPC and ATC.

lead: Four-level and five-level descriptions of UNSPSC
decision: Retain the distinction in scope
rationale: The four-level core commodity classification coexists with five-level descriptions that include an additional business layer. No parsing or forced data harmonization is performed this round.

lead: SKOS representations, download packages and mapping tables
decision: No separate count
rationale: A representation format of the same classification or a cross-system correspondence is not an additional KOS.

decision: Record historical origin without double counting
rationale: The maintainer states that PhilPapers expands MindPapers' philosophy-of-mind topics to philosophy more broadly. The old website redirects to PhilPapers.

decision: Include separately
rationale: Official documentation distinguishes the two systems: one describes the main subjects of literature, the other the domains assessed by measurement tools. This is not a version or format difference.
related_resources: APA PsycInfo Codes; APA PsycTests Codes

decision: Allow flat subject schemes, explicitly labeled
rationale: Subject categories can form a classification scheme without an explicit tree. Hierarchies must not be fabricated from numbers or wording.

lead: Research platforms and their classification components
decision: Count the specific subject scheme; assess the platform and entity graph separately
rationale: Platforms such as OpenAlex, arXiv and Scopus contain multiple entity types. F1 records only subject schemes with explicit category structures.
related_resources: OpenAlex Topics; arXiv Categories; ASJC; MAG FoS

decision: One entry for the extended classification lineage; note differences between published views
rationale: The research and authors' repository describe six levels combining FORD, Science-Metrix and dynamic finer levels. The platform's current API description mainly concerns broad OECD categories and must not be treated as complete six-level data.
related_resources: SciNoBo FoS; FORD; Science-Metrix; OpenAIRE Graph

decision: Distinct resources; EuroSciVoc is primarily F1, secondarily F2
rationale: EuroSciVoc primarily organizes research-field hierarchies and extends FORD. EuroVoc is a separate subject thesaurus.

decision: Distinct resources
rationale: The former is a three-level coded classification of science and technology fields; the latter is a thesaurus for subject indexing. Sharing an institution's name does not make them the same KOS.

lead: National extensions and recodings in the DNB directory
decision: No additional count this round
rationale: ÖFOS is explicitly a national adaptation of FORD. ISCED representation conversions and regional refinements are not automatically treated as new independent systems. Primary schedules of other national education-statistics classifications were not further verified; they remain leads for future scope expansion.
related_resources: FORD; ISCED / ISCED-F; ÖFOS; Educational Subject Classification

decision: Merge / subscheme
rationale: FAO states that all ASFA concepts are already in AGROVOC and are managed as its subscheme.

decision: Merge / subscheme
rationale: Different scopes and domain subschemes within the same NALT Concept Space.

decision: Record source systems; no separate entries this round
rationale: YSO was built from both. This round uses the current combined system as the candidate unit, without denying the historical vocabularies' independence.

decision: Merge / historical versions
rationale: Official documentation states that they have been merged into one TGM vocabulary.

decision: Internal structure; no separate count
rationale: Official documentation states that Parts are not a standalone terminology. CHBS is a tool for organizing LOINC codes.

decision: Discovery/publishing platform; not a candidate
rationale: Specific vocabularies such as P01 can count; their hosting platform is not another semantic system.

decision: KOS registry; not a candidate
rationale: Used to discover and describe specific KOS. The directory itself is not treated as a KOS being compared.

decision: Merge / historical versions
rationale: Integrated into CVRMC. The companion Relationship Designators resource is maintained separately; it is only recorded as a lead, without expanding the count.

decision: Representation language/format; not a candidate
rationale: Tools for representing or exchanging KOS are distinguished from the concrete subject resources they represent.

decision: Lead for later verification; not a candidate this round
rationale: Targeted searches did not yield sufficiently complete identity and organization descriptions. Unverified names are excluded from the total.

decision: Historical source lead; no separate entry
rationale: Official material confirms its existence. This round includes the Chinese Classified Thesaurus; the earlier system is retained as a source lead rather than a duplicate candidate.

decision: Merge by lineage
rationale: DUL developed by simplifying DOLCE Lite-Plus and DnS. Although formal content differs, this round counts the foundational lineage once to avoid duplicating lightweight versions.

decision: Merge
rationale: gUFO is a lightweight OWL implementation of UFO. Differences are noted without counting an implementation from the same lineage as a new system.

decision: Conservative merge; historical availability requires a separate check
rationale: Recorded under the Cyc knowledge-base lineage. This search of Cyc's official website did not directly locate OpenCyc's historical release page, so current OpenCyc download availability is not claimed.

decision: Merge
rationale: Molecular function, biological process and cellular component belong to one system. Basic/Plus and OWL/OBO representations do not count separately.

decision: Merge
rationale: SOSA is a shared core and forms a related ontology system with SSN. It is not counted again as an unrelated resource.

lead: Modules of SAREF, SWEET, SPAR, CCO, FIBO and QUDT
decision: Count each as one system
rationale: These projects use cooperating modules to cover their full scope. The number of modules or files is not the number of independent KOS.
related_resources: SAREF; SWEET; SPAR; CCO; FIBO; QUDT

decision: Primary group F3, secondary group F2
rationale: It serves clinical terminology needs and also has description logic, OWL axioms and inferred relationships. Its organization through logical definitions places it in the ontology group this round.

decision: Primary group F3, secondary group F2
rationale: Although named a Thesaurus, official releases distinguish asserted/inferred OWL and formal content with role relationships. Grouping follows actual organization.

decision: Include as a lightweight ontology; distinguish from strongly axiomatized ontologies
rationale: Concrete types and properties organize Web objects and offer a comparable schema. Official documentation also states that it is not a single universal ontology.

decision: Lightweight content models in F3
rationale: They contain concrete data-resource/bibliographic entity classes and semantic relations, distinguishing them from general representation languages. Their tasks do not fully correspond to subject classification of literature.

decision: Include its rights content ontology
rationale: Count classes and relations with domain semantics, such as permissions and obligations. Policy execution engines and abstract languages are not additional KOS.

decision: Count only the spatial-object ontology component
rationale: The specification also includes query functionality. Spatial classes and relations can be candidates; the query language and implementation software are not counted separately.

decision: Representation language/metamodel; excluded from candidate counts
rationale: These are specifications for representing KOS. Encoding a subject hierarchy in OWL does not automatically make it a strongly axiomatized ontology.

decision: Discovery channel; not counted as a KOS
rationale: They collect, register or provide browsing across multiple systems. The directory platform itself is distinct from an organized system of domain concepts.

decision: Include as a relation content ontology
rationale: Concrete biomedical relations such as part_of and their axioms are reusable content, distinct from general syntax for expressing relations.

decision: Include separately and record reuse relationships
rationale: Mondo integrates multiple disease sources and is more than a format conversion or version of DOID. Imported items must not be counted as original contributions.

decision: Include separately
rationale: PO organizes plant anatomy and development; TO organizes plant traits. Their conceptual objects and maintenance systems differ.

decision: Include separately
rationale: They respectively organize chemical entities, experimental methods and chemical information/descriptors; they are not serializations of the same ontology.

decision: FrameBase primarily in F3; FrameNet in the lexical-frame group
rationale: FrameBase constructs a knowledge-representation schema from frame content and supports n-ary relations. It is more than another file format, but derived reuse must be stated.

decision: Primary F1, secondary F3
rationale: Their main objects are research topics, chemical categories, policy research topics and academic disciplines, respectively. Topic/category hierarchies are the primary organizational basis; the word ontology or OWL format alone does not place them in F3.

decision: Primary F3, secondary F1
rationale: Beyond discipline hierarchies, it explicitly models phenomena, discoveries, scientists and instruments, together with property restrictions, disjointness, equivalence and axiomatic relations.

decision: Count only ChemOnt as a system
rationale: ClassyFire is an automated classification service and program using ChemOnt. The tool and its category system cannot be counted as two KOS.

decision: Count only the VIVO ontology
rationale: VIVO software, its ontology and multiple institutional installations are not separate independent systems. This round compares only the content schema for scholarly activities.

decision: Include separately; mark their industrial foundation roles
rationale: Their sources and released models are independent. The IDO material reviewed is an ISO final draft; IOF Core is a mid-level core under BFO. They cannot be merged solely because both concern industry.

lead: Integrated ontologies such as COB and SRAO
decision: Include as distinct application systems, with imported reuse labeled
rationale: They have their own integration goals and organization. Candidate-system counts are not counts of independent original knowledge sources; subsequent concept statistics must remove duplicate imports.

lead: Source leads such as DRAO, OMIT and BAO
decision: Record for later tracing; not counted as verified candidates this round
rationale: Discovered in SRAO/ModSci source descriptions, but their distinct objects, class relations and project sources have not been individually checked. They cannot yet be counted as reviewed entries.

lead: WordNet language implementations, annual versions and Open English Wordnet
decision: Consolidate
rationale: Count the system rather than each language implementation or annual dump. OEWN explicitly derives from Princeton WordNet. Language implementations may be maintained independently; they can be separated later if language differences are compared.

decision: Retain as a candidate with restricted access
rationale: Its entity-graph status is clear, but the official API returns matching entities rather than the complete interconnected graph. This round catalogs systems without promising downloadable samples.

decision: Keep as a boundary case, outside the main table for now
rationale: The original work mainly presents a link-prediction benchmark framework. Its generated KG could be listed separately in a later comparison of ready-made graph data; the framework itself is not automatically treated as an independent KOS here.

decision: Excluded
rationale: Officially described as a general research full-text corpus. Structured bibliography/citations and text do not automatically constitute an independent conceptual organization system.

decision: Boundary case for now; outside the main table
rationale: The official evidence obtained mainly concerns paper, author, citation and journal metadata. An independent concept/domain-relation schema was not verified. The word Graph alone is insufficient for inclusion.

decision: Handled by the F3 search branch
rationale: The official schema converts FrameNet frames and relations into an RDFS schema, supporting primary F3 and secondary F5 assignment. This avoids double counting across search branches.

decision: Exclude corpora; retain frame lexicons
rationale: Sense–role definitions form an independently identifiable semantic organization resource. Labeled sentences are usage instances, not additional systems.

decision: Not counted as a KOS
rationale: Knowledge-generation models associated with ATOMIC must be distinguished from symbolic knowledge graphs when counting.

decision: Not counted as a KOS; retain the USAS tagset
rationale: The tools perform annotation and analysis. The candidate is the semantic tag system and lexical correspondences they use.

decision: Discovered this round but not included in the main table
rationale: The original paper on a lexical combinatorial resource was found, but boundaries for consolidation with the existing WordNet family and VerbAtlas have not been checked fully. Retain the lead for the next round.

decision: Merge into Wiktionary as a structured derivative
rationale: The evidence supports extraction from Wiktionary into RDF/OntoLex. It does not establish an additional independent conceptual organization system.
